name: libavro
listed_description: Implementation of the Avro data serialization system.
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline. lang/c/tests/performance.c only times Avro C's own schema-resolution modes (matched schemas, resolved reader, resolved writer, complex record) and prints its own tests per second; lang/c/docs/index.txt says only 'compact, fast, binary data format' (directional, no numbers). WebSearch found only Avro C++ against msgpack C++ and protobuf in cpp-serializers style shootouts (a different implementation, avro 1.7.7, slower than msgpack) and no avro-c vs msgpack-c numbers.

name: libconcurrent
listed_description: Concurrent programming library, using coroutines, for C.
reason: README and examples/many_context1.c report only absolute numbers for its own context switch (125 ns per resume/yield on Xeon E3 2.5GHz, 954 ns on Raspberry Pi 2) with no baseline run; the 'VS.' section is a bare list of other coroutine libraries with no numbers. Search results (snippets only, aggregator blogs) place the 125 ns figure beside faster libraries (libaco, libco, boost.context) without any measurement of libconcurrent against them. Last commit 2021-09-28.

name: libcork
listed_description: Utility functions and structures, designed for resource-constrained systems. Can be embedded.
reason: README describes a simple, embeddable cross-platform C library comparable in scope to glib or APR; neither the README, docs directory listing nor any search result carried a benchmark or any performance number against a baseline. Last commit 2020-06-29.

name: libcsptr
reason: README contains no performance claim or number and no comparison with std::shared_ptr or any other reference counting implementation; the FAQ and linked blog post describe design only. Web search found only generic C++ shared_ptr overhead articles, none measuring libcsptr.

name: LibDEEP
reason: README and all wiki pages (Home, Techniques-included, Examples-of-scripts, Additional-information, TO-DO) describe RBM, DBM, DBN, EPNN, regression and PCA techniques and usage only; no timing, speedup or baseline library (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Caffe, Matlab) is mentioned. The papers/ directory holds reference papers on RBM and EPNN techniques, not speed comparisons. No third-party benchmark found.
